newsitem.title: FRANCE: Outlook downcast for Alcatel's French CIT unit.
newsitem.headline: Outlook downcast for Alcatel's French CIT unit.

text.p: Alcatel-CIT, the French telecommunications unit responsible for part of Alcatel Alsthom's huge 1995 loss, is set to unveil to its workers on Wednesday that the outlook will be downcast until 1998.
An official for the unit said on Tuesday the company, which has difficulties adjusting to a changed buying policy of its main client France Telecom, should return to break-even in 1999.
"In 1999, we should return to equilibrium," he said.
The central works council, meeting on Wednesday and Thursday, will be told there could be lay-offs.
"On the basis of the figures we have today, with our forecasts of the work load, we could have 1,634 jobs too many at the end of 1998," the official said.
At the moment the company employs 9,778 people.

The company denied rumours it wanted to close entire sites but it will shut parts of factories at Lannion, Ormes and Orvault while concentrating production at Eu, in Normandie, which it considers on of the most modern factories of the industry in Europe.

France Telecom is adapting to a competitive environment and has put price pressure on Alcatel-CIT and is also entertaining relationships with other suppliers. A similar changed attitude by Deutsche Telekom caused big losses at Alcatel's German unit Alcatel-SEL in 1994 and 1995.
